title: 'Heartbeat of Chepauk': Dhoni's Own Farewell Post Leads a Day of Tributes
excerpt: A day after CSK confirmed his IPL retirement, Dhoni broke three years of Instagram silence with the song he first used in 2020 — and teammates, rivals and a chief minister answered in kind.
body:
• MS Dhoni broke more than three years of Instagram silence on November 17 with a career montage captioned "Fans proved me wrong," hours after Chennai Super Kings confirmed his IPL retirement, The Sports Tak reported.
  • Suresh Raina called Dhoni's legacy "forever the heartbeat of Chepauk," while Rohit Sharma, Dhanush, Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin were among those who posted tributes.
  • CSK marked the moment on X with "It's 19:29… #ForOurThala" — 19:29 was the minute at which Dhoni announced his international retirement in 2020, The Sports Tak reported.
  • Dhoni, 45, stays with CSK as Team Mentor for IPL 2027; the squad, led by Ruturaj Gaikwad, heads into the December 16 mini-auction in Goa.

Chennai Super Kings confirmed MS Dhoni's retirement as an IPL player on Tuesday, November 17, and the franchise will keep him as Team Mentor from IPL 2027. What followed was less an announcement than a roll call: within a day, former teammates, rival franchises, film stars and a chief minister had posted their own farewells to the 45-year-old, according to Cricket Times.

His own words came first

Dhoni himself posted before most of the tributes landed. Hours after CSK's confirmation, he shared an emotional montage of career highlights on Instagram — his first post on the platform in over three years — captioned "Fans proved me wrong, no better song to accept it. Maybe two versions were made so that I could commit the mistake and then accept it," The Sports Tak reported. Within 15 minutes, the post had surged past two million likes. The caption refers to the song behind his 2020 international retirement post, "Main Pal Do Pal Ka Shayar Hoon" — a poet of a fleeting moment; the farewell montage used the alternate version, "Main Har Ek Pal Ka Shayar Hoon," a poet of every moment.

CSK answered in the same code. "It's 19:29… #ForOurThala," the franchise posted on X — 19:29 IST was the time of Dhoni's 2020 retirement post, The Sports Tak reported.

Teammates

"The No. 7 jersey may no longer walk onto the field, but your legacy will forever be the heartbeat of Chepauk. Once a captain, forever our Thala."

— Suresh Raina, on X

Raina, Dhoni's long-time CSK deputy, wrote that "some partnerships go beyond cricket" and that the role changing did not change the legacy. Rohit Sharma, who captained India after Dhoni, posted: "Congratulations on an incredible IPL career, Dhoni bhai. It's been fun sharing the field and so many memories with you over the years. Much respect!" Shikhar Dhawan wrote that Dhoni's "leadership, calmness and impact on the game have inspired generations," and Yuzvendra Chahal thanked him for his India debut cap: "Your guidance, mentorship and unwavering belief have played an invaluable role in shaping my journey."

Rivals and the wider world

The tributes crossed team colours. Royal Challengers Bengaluru wrote: "For the joy you gave every fan, in every colour, and for the way you carried the game, thank you, Mahi bhai." Kolkata Knight Riders posted "The helicopter lands one final time," Mumbai Indians "We've come a long way from where we began!" and Kevin Pietersen welcomed him to "the mentoring world" with a joke about contract breaks. Actor Dhanush wrote: "Some players entertain us. Some become a part of our lives. MS Dhoni has been both." Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin wrote that Dhoni "gave Chennai much more than trophies. He gave us an emotion that united generations," and BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla credited Dhoni as "an integral part of the IPL's growth and success."

What changes at CSK

The tributes rest on a record the franchise built over 19 seasons: five IPL championships and two Champions League T20 titles under Dhoni's leadership, Cricket Times noted. The playing chapter is closed, but the dugout chapter opens immediately — Dhoni mentors a squad captained by Ruturaj Gaikwad into the IPL 2027 mini-auction in Goa on December 16, The Sports Tak reported. The No. 7 jersey will not walk onto the field again; the man who wore it will be sitting a few metres away.
